[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Collections, Namespaces, and ansible-galaxy"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ansible Collections are a packaging format for distributing content that can include playbooks, roles, modules, and plugins. Understanding how namespaces work and how to utilize the ansible-galaxy command-line tool is essential for modern Ansible automation."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Namespaces and Collections"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A collection is always identified by a namespace and a collection name, separated by a dot. The namespace represents the author, organization, or business unit, while the collection name defines the specific set of modules and roles."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Namespace: A unique identifier representing the publisher (e.g., cisco, amazon, community)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Collection Name: The functional grouping of content (e.g., ios, aws, general)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Fully Qualified Collection Name (FQCN): The complete reference combining namespace and collection, such as cisco.ios."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Initializing a New Collection"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create the skeleton structure of a new collection using the ansible-galaxy command. This sets up the required directories for roles, plugins, and meta files."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"ansible-galaxy collection init my_namespace.my_collection"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Installing Collections"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"To download and install collections from Galaxy or an automation hub, use the install subcommand. You can install a single collection or list multiple requirements in a requirements.yml file."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"ansible-galaxy collection install amazon.aws"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"For enterprise environments, defining collections in a requirements file ensures consistent deployments across teams."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"collections:
  - name: amazon.aws
  - name: cisco.ios
    version: '1.2.0'"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Install the dependencies listed in the requirements file by executing the following command:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Building and Publishing Collections"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once you have developed your collection and populated it with tasks and roles, you can package it into a standard tarball artifact."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"ansible-galaxy collection build"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"After building the artifact, you can publish it to Ansible Galaxy or Automation Hub using an API token."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"ansible-galaxy collection publish my_namespace-my_collection-1.0.0.tar.gz --token=YOUR_API_TOKEN"}]
